<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Data and strange claims</p><h1>What makes FIFA 23 players good?</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>06 May 2023</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>The dataset contains player ratings, physical attributes, positions, clubs, and a healthy amount of columns that look useful until you inspect them.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>Can player overall rating be predicted accurately and efficiently, and which variables matter for that prediction?</p><h2>The experiment</h2><p>Elastic-net regression and boosted decision trees handle the two goals differently. The workflow cleans ordered work-rate variables, removes sparse or identifier-like fields, splits the data, and evaluates the fitted models.</p><pre><code>Overall ~ all usable player attributes</code></pre><p>The result is a model exercise first and a football verdict second. A game rating is a label produced by a system; it is not a complete theory of being good at football.</p></article></main>
